quests.instruction: Where could you read announcements that are posted on paper?
quests.hint: It's usually in a hallway, with papers pinned on it.
quests.explanation: A notice board lets everyone see news, dates, and reminders in one place.
quests.funFact: Notice boards use pins to hold papers so notices can be changed easily.

quests.instruction: Which small book do you use to write down homework and messages from your teacher?
quests.hint: You carry it home and back every day.
quests.explanation: A school diary helps you remember homework and lets teachers and families share messages.
quests.funFact: The word 'diary' comes from a Latin word meaning 'daily'.

quests.instruction: A paper about a class trip needs to go home to your family. What is it?
quests.hint: It's a note written for someone else to read.
quests.explanation: Schools send letters home so families know about trips, events, and changes.
quests.funFact: Many schools now send these messages by phone or email as well as on paper.

quests.instruction: Which tool sweeps dust and crumbs off the floor?
quests.hint: It has a long handle and bristles at the bottom.
quests.explanation: A broom gathers dust and crumbs into a pile, so they can go into the dustpan and bin.
quests.funFact: A broom works best when you sweep in short, gentle strokes.

quests.instruction: Which item wipes chalk or marker off the board?
quests.hint: It's held in your hand and rubbed over the board.
quests.explanation: A board duster cleans the board so the next lesson can start fresh.
quests.funFact: Wipe the board from top to bottom so dust falls away from your face.

quests.instruction: There are small paper scraps on the table after cutting. What should you do?
options: Leave them for others to clean 🙈
quests.hint: A clean table is better for the next person.
quests.explanation: Tidying up your scraps is part of caring for shared classrooms.
quests.funFact: Collecting scraps in a small tray while you work makes cleaning faster.

quests.instruction: Which cozy corner of the classroom has books and cushions for quiet reading?
quests.hint: The books and the soft seats are a clue.
quests.explanation: A reading corner is a place to enjoy books when your work is done.
quests.funFact: Reading for fun every day helps children become better readers.

quests.instruction: Where in the classroom do you sit with a small group to work on a project?
quests.hint: Several chairs go around it.
quests.explanation: A group table lets classmates share ideas and materials and work together.
quests.funFact: Cooperative learning, where students work in small groups, is used in classrooms worldwide.

quests.instruction: Where does a class gather to sit together on the floor for a story or discussion?
quests.hint: It's a soft area for sitting in a group.
quests.explanation: The carpet area lets everyone sit close and see the teacher or the book.
quests.funFact: In many classrooms, each child has a marked spot to sit.

quests.instruction: Which tool has a half-circle shape and measures angles?
quests.hint: It is marked with numbers from 0 to 180.
quests.explanation: A protractor shows how wide an angle is, in degrees.
quests.funFact: A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.

quests.instruction: Which tool can add big numbers quickly?
quests.hint: You press number keys and see the answer on a screen.
quests.explanation: A calculator adds, subtracts, multiplies, and divides large numbers very quickly.
quests.funFact: Early mechanical calculators used gears and wheels instead of electricity.

quests.instruction: Which classroom item can you stack and count to see how numbers combine?
quests.hint: You can count them one by one.
quests.explanation: Blocks let you see numbers as real things, so adding and subtracting are easy to see.
quests.funFact: Base-ten blocks use small cubes, rods, and flats to show ones, tens, and hundreds.

quests.instruction: Which container with pouring spout is used in science to hold and measure liquids?
quests.hint: It has marks on the side for amounts.
quests.explanation: A beaker holds liquids, and its marks show how much is inside.
quests.funFact: Beakers are made of glass or plastic that can be washed and reused.

quests.instruction: What should you wear on your face during a science experiment to protect your eyes?
quests.hint: It fits closely around your eyes.
quests.explanation: Safety goggles stop splashes and small bits from getting in your eyes.
quests.funFact: Safety goggles are worn in labs all over the world.

quests.instruction: Where do you put a seed with soil to watch it start to grow?
quests.hint: It holds soil and has holes at the bottom for water.
quests.explanation: A flowerpot holds soil and a seed, and lets extra water drain out.
quests.funFact: Most seeds start growing when they get enough water and warmth.

quests.instruction: Which quiet game with pieces on a checkered board practices thinking ahead?
quests.hint: It has a king, a queen, and many other pieces.
quests.explanation: Chess teaches you to plan your moves and think about what happens next.
quests.funFact: Chess is more than 1,000 years old.

quests.instruction: What do you do with a jigsaw puzzle?
quests.correctAnswer: Fit the pieces together to make a picture 🧩
options: Fit the pieces together to make a picture 🧩
Stack the pieces into a tall tower 🧱
Sort the pieces by color and stop there 🎨
quests.hint: Each piece has a place where it matches.
quests.explanation: A puzzle helps you notice shapes and patterns while you fit the picture together.
quests.funFact: A jigsaw puzzle can have as few as four pieces or thousands.

quests.instruction: Which toy can you stack to build towers and bridges?
quests.hint: You can pile them up as high as you can before they fall.
quests.explanation: Building blocks help you learn balance, shapes, and how to plan a build.
quests.funFact: Taller towers need a wider base to stay balanced.

quests.instruction: You have a stomachache. Where do you ask to go?
quests.hint: This room has a bed and a first aid box.
quests.explanation: The nurse's room is where you rest and get help if you feel sick or are hurt.
quests.funFact: A school nurse's kit often includes bandages, cold packs, and antiseptic wipes.

quests.instruction: You lost your jumper at school. Where might you find it?
quests.hint: It's a box of things that nobody has claimed.
quests.explanation: A lost and found box keeps items that students leave behind, so owners can claim them.
quests.funFact: Name labels can be sewn in or written with a laundry-safe marker so they last through washes.

quests.instruction: Where do you wait for the bus after school?
quests.hint: It has a sign showing where the bus will pick you up.
quests.explanation: A bus stop is the place where students gather and wait safely for their bus.
quests.funFact: A bus stop sign often shows which buses stop there.

quests.instruction: Which book has chapters and exercises that your class uses for lessons?
quests.hint: Teachers use it to plan and teach lessons.
quests.explanation: A textbook has lessons and practice exercises for a subject.
quests.funFact: Some textbooks are now also available on tablets and computers.

quests.instruction: Which sheet of paper has questions for you to answer in class?
quests.hint: You write on it, and then you give it to your teacher.
quests.explanation: A worksheet gives you practice with what you've been learning.
quests.funFact: A worksheet is sometimes called a handout or an activity sheet.

quests.instruction: What small strip keeps your place in a book when you stop reading?
quests.hint: You slide it between the pages.
quests.explanation: A bookmark holds your place, so you can come back to the right page.
quests.funFact: Bookmarks are better than folding page corners, because that can damage the book.

quests.instruction: Which part of the school do you walk up to reach the next floor?
quests.hint: One step after another takes you up.
quests.explanation: Stairs connect the floors, and you should walk on them carefully, holding the handrail.
quests.funFact: The word 'stair' comes from an Old English word meaning 'to climb'.

quests.instruction: Which part of a building helps people who can't use stairs, or who are carrying heavy things, go between floors?
quests.hint: You press a button and it takes you to another floor.
quests.explanation: An elevator carries people and things up and down. It is especially helpful for people who can't climb stairs.
quests.funFact: Elisha Otis showed a safety brake for elevators in 1854.

quests.instruction: What lets sunlight and fresh air into a classroom?
quests.hint: It is made of glass and sits in the wall.
quests.explanation: Windows let in daylight and can be opened to bring in fresh air.
quests.funFact: Natural light helps classrooms feel bright and saves electricity.

quests.instruction: A microscope and test tubes would be found in which room?
quests.hint: They are tools for experiments and close observation.
quests.explanation: The science lab is where students investigate and test things, using special tools.
quests.funFact: The first microscopes were built more than 400 years ago.

quests.instruction: A room has hoops, mats, and cones. What is it used for?
quests.hint: Think about what the equipment helps you do.
quests.explanation: These items are used for exercise and games, which is what PE lessons are about.
quests.funFact: The modern Olympic Games began in 1896.

quests.instruction: A room has shelves of paper, paints, and brushes. Which class is held there?
quests.hint: Look at what the materials let students make.
quests.explanation: Paper, paints, and brushes are materials for creating pictures in art class.
quests.funFact: Artists use lots of shades of the same color to make things look real.
